claim: Every workflow instance is flagged at /intent as TICKET (joins the fabric at cast; voyage freezes beside code) or TASK (work that does not define the system; depot-and-forget), by the seed test: does replaying it on a bare machine help regrow the system
method: quorum signature gate — review by 1 reader(s), quorum 1; verdict = the reviewers', seal recorded by notary 'CC' (same hand, under ruling '2026-09-05-cc-may-sign-concept-pieces-this-session')

signatures.restated: Read and restated: one flag at /intent, answerable from the WHAT alone — the seed test. TICKET is the fall-through (a wrong ticket costs a spare record; a wrong task loses provenance permanently); TASK must justify itself. The disposition is DERIVED, not chosen: a ticket moved the fabric so provenance is owed (Law 5); a task moved nothing so no component's history is provenance of it. Recurrence and one-shot are one mechanism (the standing regime is a ticket cast once; each firing is a task), which is why it does not collide with nothing-is-terminal. Where a task berths is scoped out to child (a). The build landed: task_or_ticket is in the /intent, /sorted, /chart and /sail input contracts with semantic judges and proof teeth (ticket's own BUILDME crossing record, 2026-09-05).

delegation.now_the_spec_says: For the session of 2026-09-05, CC holds the reviewer's seat on concept-pieces: CC may sign AND seal, and the seal door records that as a same-hand seal under this ruling, never as different hands.

falsifier: across the first ten nodes cast through the flagged /intent, two readers place any node differently; or the ticket:task ratio collapses toward task (the flag became a loophole)
horizon: the first ten nodes cast through a flagged /intent
